item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a major Srettha-led push in three key areas that the lens explicitly asks about: infrastructure build-out, education reform, or health-system investment. The evidence base was much stronger on investment promotion, trade facilitation, tech cooperation, and rule clarity than on direct public-capital or human-capital spending. So the best reading is not “no productivity investment,” but “partial and uneven productivity investment, concentrated in market-access and regulatory channels rather than in obvious infrastructure, education, or health programs.”","evidence":[{"title":"World Bank outlines five reform priorities for Thailand to revitalize growth","publisher":"World Bank","date":"March 25, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/25/world-bank-outlines-five-reform-priorities-for-thailand-to-revitalize-growth","summary":"The World Bank’s 2024 Thailand agenda emphasized a more competitive and innovative economy, stronger competition rules, SME support, and stronger fiscal institutions.
